comments.body:
Patchset 2 earned LLM-Review +1 but Verified -1. The CI failure is a real defect in this
story's own test, not a flake, and local `make verify` structurally could not have caught it.

ROOT CAUSE. CI reported 4 teardown errors of the form "New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT
during this test: ['.rebar/cache']". Only the first is mine —
test_plan_review_overlap.py::test_seeded_candidate_reaches_the_prompt_and_lands_advisory.
The other 3 (test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py, test_cli_space_form_options.py,
test_compute_validity_callers.py) are collateral: with 4 xdist workers, every worker whose
per-test baseline snapshot straddled the directory's creation reports it.

The writer is NOT find_similar or the similar-tickets index — that derives its cache from
StorePaths.rebar_dir, which is anchored to the parent of the canonical tracker, and this
module's `tracker` fixture lives under tmp_path. The writer is the Pass-1 checkpoint store:
_checkpoint_dir(ctx) in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:32-37 returns
Path(ctx.repo_root) / ".rebar" / "cache" / "plan-review" / ctx.ticket_id. These tests pass
repo_root=REPO_ROOT — the REAL checkout — deliberately, because the suite points REBAR_ROOT
at a sandbox repo and the project overlay that activates project.plan-overlap is reachable
only by naming the real checkout. So the checkpoint cache followed repo_root into the tree.

WHY LOCAL VERIFY PASSED. `.rebar/cache/` already existed in the worktree from earlier runs
of these same tests, so it was in the pollution guard's baseline and never "appeared." On
CI's clean checkout it is created fresh. This is a general lesson for this program: a green
local verify does not imply green CI when the difference is checkout cleanliness.

No precedent existed to copy. test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py also names the real
repo root, but only calls route_criteria — it never runs a batch, so it never writes
checkpoints. This story's test is the first to do both.

FIX (patchset 3). The `plan_reads` fixture now takes tmp_path and monkeypatches
rebar.llm.plan_review.checkpoints._checkpoint_dir to a per-test tmp_path directory. Both
call sites (checkpoints.py:110 and :129) read the module global, so one module-level
setattr reaches both. This also strengthens the isolation the fixture docstring already
reasons about: per-test checkpoint separation becomes structural rather than resting on the
plan nonce alone.

PROOF. Deleted `.rebar/cache/plan-review` in the worktree, ran the full module, and
confirmed the directory is NOT recreated — the absence is the assertion, not the passing
tests. Before the fix the same run demonstrably wrote
.rebar/cache/plan-review/abcd-0000-0000-0001/73c8625428fe....json.

ALSO IN PATCHSET 3. Patchset 2's single remaining advisory (tests) was correct: no test
exercised the honest-empty-match path — status 'ok' with zero candidates — which
overlap_candidates' own docstring names as the contract. Every degraded path also reports
zero candidates, so `candidates == 0` alone carries no information; only the status
discriminates. Added test_an_honest_empty_match_is_recorded_as_ok_not_as_degradation
(23 tests total). RED-proved by mutating overlap_candidates to report an empty result set
as "retrieval-error": the new test failed, and overlap.py reverted byte-identical.

lint and typecheck green. Full `make verify` running now.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criterion 5 is undelivered: plan review never tells a reviewer that the plan overlaps work another ticket describes. Each plan is read in isolation, so two tickets planning one change both pass. Create-time surfacing matches a title and short description where plan review matches a full plan, but one index serves both.

## Approach

**Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path.** The sibling story builds a lexical FTS5 index under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, caught up in the read phase. Its whole public surface is `find_similar` (`src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:46-54`), taking query text via `text=` (`:51`) and `exclude_id=` for self-hits (`:52`). With the optional embedding tier configured it ranks through that tier, else lexically (`:79-82`): no model provider is required.

**The one gap: failure distinguishability.** Every failure returns `[]`, per "Never raises" (`:55`), so a caller cannot tell an absent index from a failed catch-up from an empty match.

**Diagnostic contract.** `find_similar` gains one keyword-only parameter `diagnostics: dict | None = None`; given a dict it records a single `status`. The set is closed, one value per branch: `index-absent` `:63`, `catch-up-failed` `:66-71`, `retrieval-error` at the outer handler `:84`, else `ok` (`:80` embedding, `:82` lexical). An embedding-provider failure is NOT a status: `embedding.rank` returns `None` for every cause it cannot serve (`:76-79`), and `:82` then serves lexical results, so that path is `ok`. Return type, "Never raises" and every existing call stay unchanged: the signal travels through the dict. The only `src/` consumer, `recent_creates.py:196`, passes none.

**Recording channel: coverage, written in place.** `run_pass1` takes `coverage` as a mutable dict (`pass1.py:238`) and assigns diagnostic keys directly -- e.g. `coverage["isf"]` `:473`; `coverage["overlap"]` is written the same way.

**Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam.** A Pass-1 finder unit already accepts store-derived `extra_context` (`checkpoints.py:54`), its identity binding that context by `context_digest`, a sha256 over the injected text (`:61-63`). That text is built by `_chunk_extra_context` (`pass1.py:215`), called at `:326`, so injection lands in `pass1.py`. The seam is already criterion-keyed -- `:219` injects G5 context when G5 is in the chunk, `:221` the no-file-impact block when that criterion is -- so overlap adds a third branch on that test, keyed to `project.plan-overlap`. Riding it rather than adding a pass leaves checkpoint identity and caching unchanged: a changed candidate set yields a different `context_digest`.

**Zero marginal LLM cost: the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging.** Candidates ride a chunk already being sent, so judging adds no LLM call; lexical retrieval is not one either. The cap is on candidates, not calls: 5, the default `RESULT_LIMIT` (`lexical.py:39`), the operating point ADR 0122 makes load-bearing.

**On demand, not on every review.** The switch is one keyword-only parameter `overlap: bool = False` on `review_plan` (`plan_review/__init__.py:199`), threaded exactly as `probe_criteria`, because `review_plan` assembles no batch request. The chain: `review_plan` -> `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` (`gate_dispatch.py:64`, called at `__init__.py:473`) -> `run_workflow` inputs (`:183`) -> a new `overlap:` input in `gates/plan-review.yaml` (`:24` declares `probe_criteria`) wired into the finders batch `with:` (`:54`, `:66`) -> `req.with_inputs` -> `ProductionBatchRunner.run` (`production_batch_runner.py:120-124`) -> `run_pass1` (`pass1.py:232`) -> `_chunk_extra_context`. Always threaded, `False` = off, so `${{ inputs.overlap }}` always resolves.

**The flag gates FAN-IN, so the off switch is total.** For a PROJECT criterion the `include_project_plan_overlap` key (`workflow_ops.py:267`) is only a coverage record: `_project_criteria` never reads it, filtering solely on the `probe` allowlist (`production_batch_runner.py:283-287`, fed at `:123`). `overlap` therefore rides beside `probe` at `:120-124`, and `_keep` gains one arm dropping the id when false. Not fanned in, the id never reaches `registry.chunk_by_facet` (`pass1.py:262`), so with `overlap=False` it sits in no chunk's rubric and is absent from `prompt_id` (`checkpoints.py:66`): checkpoint identity stays byte-identical, and no finder can emit the finding from plan text alone.

**Decision rule: posture, not prompt.** Mirroring `decomposition_state_block` (`det_lint.py:46`, shape at `:66-70`), `overlap.py` emits a `## POSSIBLE OVERLAP (from store)` heading, a directive to judge whether this plan does work a listed ticket describes, then one `alias -- title (similarity <score>)` line per candidate. Both backends return exactly `id`/`alias`/`title`/`score` (`similar/lexical.py:110-117`) and the index row (`:101`) carries no workflow status, so `score` is the only per-candidate signal available, and it is what separates a near-duplicate plan from a distant neighbour. Identity falls back to `id` when `alias` is absent. A new `project.plan-overlap` entry in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `exec: "1-TURN"`, `facet: "project-invariants"`, `default_posture: "advisory"` -- the shape `project.symbol-reference-completeness` has. `exec: "1-TURN"` attributes the finding: the fan-in above puts the id in a chunk's rubric, and `P1Finding.criteria` (`passes.py:51`) is the finder's rubric-id field, so it is tagged because it is IN the rubric, not because prose asks it. Posture then decides: the decide pass partitions findings by `decision` (`orchestrator.py:294-301`) and `_any_blocking_criterion` (`:325-330`) intersects a finding's `criteria` with blocking-posture ids only, keyed to `default_posture` (`det_invariants.py:85`), so an advisory id can never reach `blocking`.

**Degradation.** On any non-`ok` status the candidate list is empty and no overlap finding is emitted; the review proceeds normally.

**Injection site has little headroom, so work is extracted.** `pass1.py` is 658 lines against the 800 cap, so overlap retrieval and its diagnostic live in a new `plan_review/overlap.py`; `_chunk_extra_context` gains only the call.

Any ratcheted mechanism added carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket at its definition site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With `overlap=True`, reviewing a ticket whose plan restates an existing ticket's plan emits an advisory overlap finding naming that ticket; on a store seeded with over 5 matches exactly 5 candidates are injected. One seeded-store test per case.
- [x] The off switch is total, one test per case: with `overlap=False` no overlap finding is emitted; `project.plan-overlap` is absent from `coverage["batch_resolution"]["single"]`; checkpoint identity stays byte-identical to the same review before this change; with `overlap=True` the LLM call count equals the `overlap=False` count.
- [x] An overlap finding can never turn a verdict from pass to block, one test per case: it is attributed to a criterion whose routing `default_posture` is `advisory`; the decide pass places it there; a passing plan's verdict is unchanged with one present.
- [x] Two compatibility invariants, one test each: `find_similar` called without `diagnostics` returns what it did before this change (the `recent_creates.py:196` call); with no model provider configured overlap retrieval still returns lexical-tier candidates.
- [x] Degradation, one test per status (`index-absent` absent index; `catch-up-failed` catch-up raises; `retrieval-error` retrieval raises): `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` records it; the overlap finding set is empty; the verdict equals the same review with `overlap=False`.
- [x] The tree-wide gates pass, one check each: every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines (module-size gate); `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0; `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0.

file_impact.reason: find_similar gains the opt-in diagnostics dict that separates an absent index, a failed catch-up, a retrieval error and an honest empty match
new unit holding overlap retrieval, the capped candidate block and its diagnostic, because pass1.py has little headroom against the 800-line cap
_chunk_extra_context gains the overlap-context branch and run_pass1 records coverage['overlap']
review_plan gains the keyword-only overlap parameter and threads it to produce_plan_review_verdict, as the Approach section describes
overlap rides beside probe in the batch inputs and _keep drops the criterion id when it is false, which is the total-off-switch mechanism the Approach section describes
produce_plan_review_verdict passes overlap through to the run_workflow inputs, the middle link of the threading chain the Approach section enumerates
declares the new overlap workflow input and wires it into the finders batch with:, as the Approach section specifies
carries the project.plan-overlap entry whose advisory default_posture is what makes the finding non-blocking
the project-local criterion prompt, following the tracked .rebar/prompts precedent for rebar-local rules
un-ignores the new project-local prompt so it is tracked, matching the existing un-ignore entries for the other .rebar/prompts criteria
documents the on-demand overlap switch and its advisory posture

the sidecar tests for every acceptance criterion: seeding and the five-candidate cap, the total off switch, advisory posture, compatibility, each degradation status, the honest-empty case, and the tree-wide gates
